name: Glow up

lead: A glow up is a noticeable improvement in how someone looks, usually over weeks to years. The term covers everything from skincare and haircuts to fillers and rhinoplasty, and it appears across looksmax forums in thread titles such as '30 day glow up' guides and personal transformation stories.

The chain is grooming, skincare and fitness changes, then cumulative visible improvement, then a marked before-and-after difference. It is documented mostly through testimonials and photos. Published research on the term is minimal; a 2024 Frontiers in Psychiatry study named a professional photoshoot intervention for adolescent psychiatric patients 'Glow up'.

paras: Posters describe combining skincare, hydration, diet, exercise, haircuts and facial hair grooming, and sometimes cosmetic procedures. A common starting point is a generic 30-day plan covering the basics, with larger changes added over time. Some users note that better skin, lighting or photo angles also contribute to how a transformation looks.
Risks depend on the method, from none for basic grooming to those of filler and surgery. Some testimonials describe bullying, insecurity or an eating disorder as the background to a transformation.

angle.text: A glow up is a marked improvement in appearance built from small grooming, skincare and fitness changes that add up, and in some cases cosmetic procedures. It is documented mostly through testimonials and before-and-after photos.

lead: Glow up is slang for a marked improvement in a person's appearance, often shown with before-and-after photos. In looksmaxxing communities it is used both for small changes such as grooming and skincare and for large ones involving cosmetic procedures [1][2].

Most of the material comes from forum testimonials and how-to threads. One looksmax.org thread presents a generic 30-day plan covering skincare, hydration, diet, haircuts and facial hair grooming, written in the style of a general-advice list [1]. Another user's long personal account describes bullying and an eating disorder in adolescence, followed by filler in the nose, cheeks, chin, lips, jaw and under-eyes, and rhinoplasty in 2025 [2].
In the research literature the phrase appears occasionally: a 2024 Frontiers in Psychiatry study named a professional photoshoot intervention for adolescent psychiatric patients 'Glow up' [3].
infobox: Skincare, grooming, fitness, diet, cosmetic procedures

paras: Glow-up threads on looksmax.org include requests for ratings and advice, timelines such as 14 or 30 days, and long personal accounts [1][2]. Some replies are sceptical; in one thread a user remarked that people claim a glow up after only improving their skin [4].
The related term 'makeover' has a long history in television and film, covering changes to clothing, haircuts, cosmetics and sometimes weight loss or plastic surgery [5].

No studies found testing 'glow up' as a looksmaxxing method. A 2024 longitudinal intervention study in Frontiers in Psychiatry examined whether a professional photoshoot affected self-esteem and emotions in child and adolescent psychiatric patients, introducing it as a novel intervention producing visual content [3]. It examined a photoshoot, not appearance modification procedures.

lore.intro: On looksmax.org, glow ups are shared as photo transformations and how-to lists, and debated over whether the change is real [1][2][4].
